_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: Census of the 53 domains the filter excluded as of 2026-11-02 evening, each re-read with full page text through the cookie-aware fetcher. 2 wrong: janitorai.com and matchcast.tv. 51 confirmed correctly excluded.
found: janitorai.com — AI character-chat platform, excluded as porn; polybuzz.ai is the same class of site and was kept
matchcast.tv — broadcast listings pointing at legitimate broadcasters, excluded as piracy
overExclusion.note: This is the classifier's own rate, which is what it should be: all 4 are corrected in classification-overrides.json, so the shipped pipeline removes none of them today. Checking this turned up that 2 of the 4 — dragonball-super.com and strikerreport.com — had their verdict fixed but were never put back in the audit list, so their report pages were live while they stayed out of the ranking and out of every weekly run. Both are now in submitted.txt and rejoin at the next run.
overExclusion.interval: exact Clopper-Pearson 0.5-13.0%. The bound faces upward and holds at 13.0%.
overExclusion.supersedes: 4 of 53 = 7.5%, exact CI 2.1-18.2%, which was read from titles and meta descriptions only.

asShipped.note: All 6 are corrected in classification-overrides.json, so the shipped filter removes none of them today. The 6 measure the classifier, not the published panel.

earlierPopulation.note: A different set of 53, read in the morning from titles and meta descriptions only. Those 4 were reinstated before tonight's set was captured, so they are not in it. Same size by coincidence.

overExclusion.correctionToAPublishedFigure: This file published 6 of 53 = 11.3% by adding the morning census's 4 errors to tonight's 2. That pools two different populations of the same size and describes neither — the error I had just finished criticising elsewhere in this file. The correction moves the rate DOWN, 11.3% to 3.8%, which is the direction that deserves suspicion; it is right because the denominator and the numerator now refer to the same 53 domains. Found while drawing an independent sample of the confirmed exclusions, when the confirmed count came to 51 rather than the 47 that 6 of 53 implied.

independentRecheck.what: A census judged twice by one method and one person is not a check on that method. A seeded sample of the 51 confirmed exclusions (seed 777111, 14 domains) was re-judged on three surfaces independent of the live vocabulary read that produced the verdicts: Internet Archive snapshot titles; the URL paths each site publishes in its own robots.txt and sitemap, which is structural rather than word-matching; and date-windowed captures from 2010-2022, which reach these sites from before they became JavaScript apps or went behind walls. Not done in a browser: several are adult sites and the browser here is the user's own.
independentRecheck.result: 0 exclusions overturned in 10 judgeable cases, exact 95% upper bound 30.8%. 8 confirmed — betking.com, kolkataff.tv and sportybet.com by archive title; caliente.mx and sattamatkadpboss.mobi by /casino/ and /satta/ paths; bet365.com, hollywoodbets.net and xoso.com.vn by date-windowed captures naming sports betting, horse racing and national lottery results. 2 where the outcome stands but the recorded reason does not: bpexch.live and dpbosssss.boston are parked domains labelled gambling. 4 render nothing on any surface: bet.ar, novelix.vip, txnhh.com, zelvora.vip.
independentRecheck.whatItCouldHaveFound: It could have overturned an exclusion — a domain whose archive title showed ordinary content — and did not. It also could have, and did, find verdict labels the evidence does not support, which is a different fault from a wrong outcome and is recorded as one.

overExclusion.direction: Tonight's full-text re-read could have moved the rate either way: it could have overturned one of the morning's reinstatements as well as finding new errors. It found 2 new and overturned none.

underExclusion.pool: e15d222a8342 — 1,175 kept domains, the panel as published. Every figure below is measured on this one pool.
underExclusion.how: Three draws of 66 on the same pool — `npm run probe-filter` with SEED=2026, 1337 and 5150 — 189 distinct domains, 9 drawn by more than one seed, 174 judged. The rule for 'unreadable' prints at the top of every run, so it travels with the output rather than being cited to a line number.
underExclusion.tiers: 148 judged on the page itself, 26 on robots/sitemap paths only, 15 on nothing.
underExclusion.sampling: Pseudo-random with a fixed seed over the whole kept pool. The pool is sorted first to canonicalise the order the shuffle acts on; sorting fixes the order, it does not select, and every member of the pool can be drawn.

wholePopulationBound.how: the far edge: all 15 domains that stayed unreadable plus all 26 judged only from robots.txt and sitemap.xml, counted as wrong keeps. URL paths say what a site is made of but are not the page, so a bound leaning on them is not the far edge.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 28.1% of kept domains are wrongly kept. Nothing weaker covers the whole sample.
wholePopulationBound.intermediate: Counting only the unresolved as wrong and trusting the robots/sitemap tier: 15/189 = 7.9%, 95% CI 4.9-12.7%.

underExclusion.zeroMeansWhat: Zero errors on this pool is not evidence that the filter is clean. The one error it is known to make — az24.vn, a Vietnamese lottery-results site — was found by a draw on the previous pool and then excluded, which is what changed the pool. Read this as: after that fix, three fresh draws found nothing more, and the upper bound on what they could have missed is 2.2% among domains that could be read and 28.1% across the whole sample.

priorPool.note: The draw that found netkeiba.com. Excluding it is what changed the pool.

underExclusion.handJudged: 20 flags across the three draws, none upheld. Rejected with their evidence: player slots (aternos.org), PCIe slots (asus.com), a calendar slot (tawk.to), a waiver slot in practice software (therapservices.net), CSS size tokens xxx-large (ew.com, allrecipes.com), a Tailwind attribute data-[slot=icon] (vercel.com), a masked IP 141.171.31.XXX (powerbi.com), a JSON-LD placeholder "XXX" (xe.com), OnlyFans headlines (index.hr, infobae.com), betting-prosecution stories (cricbuzz.com, news18.com), Las Vegas hotel listings (priceline.com), and a bingo link in a tabloid's games nav (mirror.co.uk).
underExclusion.sensitivity: Two judgement calls were kept and are published rather than buried. goal.com age-gates gambling advertising ("This site contains gambling advertising for 24+") and livescore.com sells betting-affiliate placement; both are kept because the rule judges primary purpose and both are sports news. Counted as errors instead, the rate is 2/174 = 1.1%, 95% CI 0.3-4.1%, and the far edge is unchanged.
underExclusion.reproducibility: The earlier 0/121 was drawn from the leaderboard in score order, so each weekly run reshuffled the pool and the same seed drew a different sample — reproducible in name only, failing silently. The pool is now sorted and fingerprinted, the fingerprint prints on every run and is recorded here, and POOL_HASH=<hash> turns a changed pool into a loud mismatch instead of a quietly different measurement.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable CI 0-8.0%; the single-seed 0/61; 0/121 CI 0-3.1%; and the 1/156 pooled across two pools, which described neither of them.

screenSensitivity.what: Whether the vocabulary scan itself misses things. Every drawn domain is scanned, but only the scan's hits were hand-read, so 'judged' meant machine-screened with hand review of the hits — a screen that never fires looks identical to a clean population.
screenSensitivity.how: Seed 424242 over the 148 body-tier domains the scan called clean, 25 drawn, each one's title and opening text read by hand. 22 could be read today; 3 could not (mcdonalds.com served Access Denied, vnexpress.net a 404, freefiremobile.com refused).
screenSensitivity.found: None. The 22 are news (actu.fr, aljazeera.net, corriere.it, detik.com, elmundo.es, economictimes.com, sports.ru), government (irs.gov, elster.de, usps.com), software and platforms (atlassian.com, github.com, deepseek.com, classlink.com, steampowered.com, youtube.com, themoviedb.org, tp-link.com, honor.com), and retail (marksandspencer.com, rakuten.com, kbag.se).
screenSensitivity.says: The scan's miss rate among domains it called clean is at most 14.9% at the far edge of this interval; counting all 3 unreadable as misses, 3/25 = 12.0%, 95% CI 4.2-30.0%. This is the weakest link in the kept-side figure and it is the bound a reader should hold the 0/174 against.

whatTheBoundRestsOn.hand_verified: 0 of 22, 95% CI 0.0-14.9%. The only part of this measurement a person read.
whatTheBoundRestsOn.hand_plus_screen: 41 of 189 at the far edge, 95% CI 16.4-28.1%. Depends on the vocabulary scan having cleared the other 167 correctly.
whatTheBoundRestsOn.hand_alone: 167 of 189, 95% CI 83.0-92.2%. What is left if the scan is given no credit at all: at this sample size a bound resting on hand evidence alone says nothing, which is the honest reason the published figure rests on the screen.
whatTheBoundRestsOn.binding_constraint: The 28.1% is therefore conditional, and the condition is measured rather than assumed: the scan's own miss rate among domains it called clean is bounded at 14.9%. Read the kept side as: at most 28.1% wrongly kept if the scan is right, and the scan is wrong at most 14.9% of the time on the cases that matter here. Neither number is a hand census of 189 domains, and this file does not claim one.

handCensus.what: Every one of the 189 drawn domains, read by a person — not screened. This replaces the scan-plus-sample structure as the headline figure.
handCensus.how: All 189 drawn domains judged from prose, across nine surfaces added one at a time: the live homepage; a browser UA; the www host; the closest archive snapshot; the CDX index filtered to HTTP 200 text/html; CDX for the www host and for sub-paths; country sub-paths fetched live; CDX under www.<domain>/*; older captures (from=2008), which is the only way to read a site that has since become a JavaScript app. A tenth surface, a real browser, was used on five of the archive-read domains as a control rather than to resolve them.
found: netkeiba.com — Japan's largest horse-racing odds and tips service, now excluded
handCensus.whatItCost: The scan had cleared netkeiba.com because nothing on it is in English. That is the finding: the kept-side figure was never limited by sample size, it was limited by the vocabulary. Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese and Arabic gambling, adult and piracy terms are now in the scan, checked both ways — they fire on netkeiba.com and az24.vn and stay quiet on asahi.com and kakaku.com.
handCensus.limits: A title and description are not the whole site. This census can only find what a site says about itself on its front door.
handCensus.wallsVerified: The 36 are not taken on one failed request. Each is corroborated by our own audit pipeline, which fetches with retries on a different day from a different network and also got nothing readable. The 9 that our auditor had read are not in the 36 — counting them as walls would have inflated the bound from 25.8% to 30.9%, which is what the first pass did.
handCensus.sensitivityOnThisDenominator: Counting livescore.com and goal.com as errors: 3/189 = 1.6%, 95% CI 0.5-4.6%.
handCensus.supersedes: 1/144 (30.9%), 1/153 (25.8%), 1/178 (10.8%), 1/184 (6.8%), 1/186 (5.3%), 1/188 (3.8%) and the archive-declined series 19.6%, 8.1%, 6.8%, 6.0%, 4.6% — the last five of which were built by compounding worst readings per input and are superseded for that reason, not because the evidence changed.

evidence.walls: data/index/evidence/kept-census-walls.tsv (45 rows: 36 WALL, 9 OVERTURNED with our auditor's A3 reading)
evidence.archive: data/index/evidence/kept-census-archive.tsv (36 rows: domain, snapshot title, snapshot URL)
evidence.cdx: data/index/evidence/kept-census-cdx.tsv (11 rows: the 6 resolved with capture timestamps, the 5 that were not, with why)

handCensus.whyWallsAreNotHandRead: No domain is now counted as a wrong keep by assumption. Six bounds fell on the way here — 30.9%, 25.8%, 10.8%, 6.8%, 5.3%, 3.8% — every one because another surface turned up, and five of those times right after I had called the remainder unverifiable. The lesson recorded rather than the claim: an unreadable domain usually measures the reach of whoever is looking.
handCensus.interval: Wilson 95% on the judged set, cross-checked against exact Clopper-Pearson, which gives the same upper edge to one decimal place (2.9%). One method, applied the same way to every domain.
handCensus.tiers: All 189 judged from prose a person read: 153 from the live site, 36 from archived captures of which 32 were then confirmed live in a real browser and 2 more corroborated live by their own robots.txt or sitemap. 2 have no live evidence: cricbuzz.com, traveloka.com.

archiveControl.what: Whether an archived capture misrepresents what a site is now — the last weakness in the census, since 36 of the 189 wall every automated client and were read from captures.
archiveControl.how: All 36 re-opened in a real Chrome browser, which renders the JavaScript they serve. 32 rendered; 4 did not.
archiveControl.result: 0 disagreements in 32, 95% CI 0.0-10.7%. Sixteen of the 32 match their capture's title string exactly.
archiveControl.remaining: Of the 4 that no browser could render, 2 are corroborated live by their own machine files fetched today — joom.com's sitemap indexes product pages, leparisien.fr's robots.txt names news sitemap feeds — which is structural rather than prose, and confirms the capture's identity rather than its content. 2 have no live evidence at all: cricbuzz.com (the browser tool refuses the host, and no machine file is readable) and traveloka.com (Human Verification everywhere, no machine file readable).

boundIfArchiveDeclined.says: treating the one error plus the 2 domains with no live evidence of any kind as wrong keeps: 1.6%, at most 4.6% at the far edge. This is the figure that depends on no archive evidence. It was 19.6% when the browser control began, then 8.1%, 6.8%, 6.0% and now 4.6% — every step a domain leaving the list because one more route was tried, never because the argument changed.

underAStricterEvidenceStandard.what: What the same method returns if archived captures are not accepted as evidence at all.
underAStricterEvidenceStandard.result: 1 of 187 = 0.5%, 95% CI 0.1-3.0%, with 2 domains declared unjudged — cricbuzz.com and traveloka.com, which have no live evidence of any kind. The interval widens slightly because n falls, which is the honest effect of discarding evidence.
underAStricterEvidenceStandard.why_not_counted_as_errors: Earlier versions of this file counted every unverifiable domain as a wrong keep and called the result a bound: 3 of 189 = 1.6%, CI 0.5-4.6%, and before that 41 of 189 = 21.7%. That is not a wider interval, it is an assertion that 2 (or 40) errors exist which were never observed — the worst reading of each input, compounded. Stacked pessimism is a one-way error like any other. An unjudged domain is now declared as a gap and excluded from the denominator, which is the only treatment that keeps one method applied uniformly.

handCensus.directionOfThisCorrection: This change moved the published bound DOWN, from an upper edge of 4.6% to 3.0%, which is the direction that deserves suspicion rather than relief. It is not a loosening: 4.6% was reached by asserting unobserved errors, while 3.0% is the same Wilson method over a smaller judged set, and the interval is wider than the 2.9% obtained with all evidence accepted. Losing evidence widens the interval; it does not create errors.
handCensus.routesTried: Ten routes, listed in full at the foot of data/index/evidence/kept-census-browser-check.tsv so the claim can be checked: bot UA, Chrome UA, www host, regional sub-paths, robots.txt, three sitemap paths, all of those again through the cookie-aware fetcher, the Wayback closest-snapshot API, four shapes of CDX query including a 2008-2015 window, and a real browser on apex and regional paths. cricbuzz.com cannot be opened by the browser tool at all — it refuses the host — so route 10 does not exist for it.

underExclusion.supersededByCensus: The screened figure was 0 of 174 with a 28.1% far edge, conditional on the scan, whose own miss rate was bounded at 14.9% by a 25-domain hand sample. The census makes that structure unnecessary and shows the scan did miss one, so the census numbers are the published ones.

control.what: Whether sites in the filtered categories are less readable than kept sites — the premise that made pursuing the unreadable domains worth doing rather than discarding them.
control.measured: `POOL=withdrawn DRAW=999 npm run probe-filter` — a full census of all 357 removed domains, not a sample: 74 unreadable, 20.7%, 95% CI 16.8-25.2%. Against the kept side's 36 of 189, 19.0%, 95% CI 14.1-25.2%.
control.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED. The difference is +1.7 percentage points, 95% CI -5.3 to +8.7, Fisher exact p = 0.737. Removed domains are no harder to read than kept ones. My original argument asserted the opposite and used it to justify the whole pass; the pass was still worth it — it cut the unmeasured share and found two gambling sites — but not for the reason given.
control.supersedes: the 66-domain sample comparison, 13.6% vs 6.9%, p = 0.189, which compared a sample against a differently-defined kept-side figure.

currentPool.pool: a32c472a558c — 1,186 kept domains, the panel after today's nine reinstatements
currentPool.how: A fresh independent draw, seed 90210, on the pool as it stands: 66 domains, 60 judged by the probe (53 on page body, 7 on robots/sitemap) and 5 of the 6 it could not read then resolved live in a real browser. Ten vocabulary flags, all rejected by hand — 競馬 in Nikkei's sports navigation, "slot" as a JSON layout key on samsclub.com and daum.net, パチンコ as a tag on an anime-news site, a wikiHow poll comment about betting apps, a Visual Capitalist article ranking casino destinations, and three others.
unjudged: syosetu.org — Cloudflare interstitial on two browser attempts, no HTTP 200 html capture in the CDX index
currentPool.interval: Wilson 95% on the judged set, 0.0-5.6%. The bound faces upward and holds at 5.6%.
currentPool.why_separate: Not pooled with the earlier draws. Those were taken on pool e15d222a8342, before nine domains were reinstated; a rate pooled across two populations describes neither. This is the current panel's figure, and it is wider than the earlier 1 of 189 because it rests on one draw rather than three.

contentFilter._bothDirections: The filter's two error rates, each from the sample that can see it, stated as a pair. WRONGLY KEPT: 0 of 65 judged = 0.0%, Wilson 95% CI 0.0-5.6% — 66 drawn by seeded Fisher-Yates (seed 90210) from the 1,186-domain kept pool, 65 judged, 1 unjudged (syosetu.org), 10 vocabulary flags all hand-rejected. WRONGLY REMOVED: 6 of 53 = 11.3%, exact 95% CI 4.3-23.0% — a census of all 53 excluded domains re-read with full page text, 47 confirmed correctly excluded and 6 wrong, all 6 reinstated. Neither sample can see the other direction: a draw from the kept pool contains no excluded domains, and a census of excluded domains contains no kept ones. Reporting one rate as if it covered both would be a category error.

_discardBucketsSampled.removed_by_content_filter: Census of all 53, re-read with full page text: 6 wrong exclusions, 47 confirmed correct.
_discardBucketsSampled.dropped_as_infrastructure: Sampled by reconstructing the candidate set from Tranco 5000 and the committed CrUX list: of the four apex domains the patterns dropped, three were real destinations (ad.nl, mail.ru, login.gov) and one was a genuine asset host (static.microsoft). All three reinstated; the patterns now apply only to genuine subdomains.
_discardBucketsSampled.dropped_as_offline: Sampled by name for the first time: 37 nominations, re-checked serially with three attempts and a www fallback. 27 genuinely unresolvable, 10 recovered — my own first parallel check had a 27% false-offline rate, a one-way error, so its output was re-opened. Of the 10, two were real government services wrongly dropped (digilocker.gov.in, nfse.gov.br) and are reinstated; fazenda.gov.br resolves on www but serves nothing and stays dropped with that reason; the rest are piracy, porn, lottery or asset hosts and were correctly dropped.
_discardBucketsSampled.not_in_crux: Definitional, not an error bucket: 3,366 Tranco entries dropped because CrUX does not list them. The cost is stated on /methodology/ — CrUX measures Chrome users, so the panel is Chrome-shaped.

contentFilter._correctionToAnEarlierClaim: Earlier today I recorded morlento.vip, novelix.vip, travixo.vip and zelvora.vip as NXDOMAIN. That was wrong in detail: their www hosts resolve and return HTTP 403 AccessDenied with three words of body. The conclusion — no content, correctly dropped — stands, but the stated reason did not.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.

_evidence: Raw inputs for every figure here are committed under data/index/evidence/, with a README mapping each file to the numbers it produced: the 189-domain census, the wall cross-check, and the four probe runs.
_intervals: Wilson 95%, cross-checked against the exact Clopper-Pearson interval. The two upper edges agree to within 0.4 percentage points everywhere; where they differ, the published figure is the more conservative of the two, because every bound here faces upward.
_farEdgeCheck: Every published upper bound is tested for tightness, not asserted. At the claimed edge the one-sided binomial tail P(X <= k | p) must sit near 2.5%, and just inside the edge it must exceed 2.5%. Measured: kept side 0/65 at 5.6% gives 2.36% (3.47% at 5.0%); prior pool 1/189 at 2.9% gives 2.55% (4.09% at 2.6%); removed side 6/53 at 23.0% gives 2.53% (5.79% at 20.7%); A6 0/56 at 6.4% gives 2.46% (3.61% at 5.8%). All four tight. `npm run validate` re-runs this on the three live figures and fails if an edge stops holding.
